title: Finding Is Not Returning, Returning Is Not Reconstructing: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Agent Social Re-entry
abstract: arXiv:2610.39781v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly participate in persistent social environments, understanding their long-term social interaction capabilities becomes increasingly important. While existing research has advanced long-term memory and conversational context retrieval, less attention has been paid to whether agents can autonomously re-engage with previously inactive conversations. In particular, remembering a past interaction does not necessarily mean that an agent can identify when to revisit it, decide to return, or reconstruct the context needed for a coherent continuation. To investigate this gap, we introduce agent social re-entry as a multi- dimensional evaluation problem, distinguishing three complementary capabilities: Finding, Returning, and Reconstructing. We develop a shared-snapshot evaluation framework that measures these dimensions independently, allowing us to examine how conversational resurfacing and persist

translated_title: 发现不等于返回，返回不等于重构：智能体社交重返的多维度评估
translated_abstract: 随着大型语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地参与持久化的社交环境，理解其长期社交交互能力变得日益重要。尽管现有研究在长期记忆和对话上下文检索方面取得了进展，但对智能体能否自主重新接入先前不活跃的对话却关注较少。尤其是，记住过去的交互并不一定意味着智能体能够识别何时需要重新查看该交互、决定返回，或重构实现连贯延续所需的上下文。为探究这一空白，我们将智能体社交重返定义为一个多维度评估问题，区分出三种互补能力：发现、返回与重构。我们开发了一个共享快照评估框架来独立测量这些维度，使我们能够考察对话的重新浮现与持续……
tldr: 该论文提出“智能体社交重返”这一多维度评估问题，将智能体重新接入历史对话的能力分解为“发现”、“返回”与“重构”三种互补能力，并开发共享快照评估框架对其进行独立测量。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "agent social re-entry" as a multi-dimensional evaluation problem, decomposing agents' ability to re-engage with past conversations into three complementary capabilities—Finding, Returning, and Reconstructing—and develops a shared-snapshot evaluation framework to measure them independently.
